sourceArticle.title: ArrowJS Reaches 1.0, Recast as the First UI Framework for the Agentic Era
sourceArticle.author: Daniel Curtis

athenaOutput.directive: Establish ArrowJS as the zero-friction, zero-build UI layer for the Creative Liberation Engine, enabling instantaneous, agent-generated interfaces that bypass traditional compilation bottlenecks.
athenaOutput.rationale: The Agentic Era demands a paradigm shift in UI generation. Traditional frameworks (React, Vue) require heavy build steps (Vite, Webpack), introducing latency that violates Article XX (Zero human wait time). ArrowJS uses native ES modules and template literals—structures that LLMs manipulate flawlessly natively. By adopting ArrowJS, agents can write, inject, and execute reactive UI components in real-time, treating interfaces as dynamic, disposable, and instantly verifiable artifacts.

options.title: The Zero-Build Agentic Canvas
options.description: Utilize ArrowJS to allow agents like BOLT to generate raw `.js` and `.html` files that are immediately served to the browser without any compilation step. Agents write reactive state and template strings directly, achieving sub-second UI rendering.
options.tradeoffs: Sacrifices the massive existing React/Vue component ecosystem. Requires the Creative Liberation Engine to establish and enforce its own strict UI primitives from scratch to maintain quality.

options.title: Ephemeral, Task-Specific UIs
options.description: Shift from monolithic dashboards to 'throwaway' interfaces. When a user requests data or a specific tool, the engine generates a bespoke ArrowJS interface for that exact moment, discarding it when the task is complete.
options.tradeoffs: High risk of visual fragmentation and inconsistent UX if agents do not strictly adhere to design tokens. Ephemeral states make debugging historical actions difficult.

options.title: The 'String-Native' Component Registry
options.description: Build a comprehensive library of ArrowJS components specifically optimized for LLM consumption. Since ArrowJS relies on template literals, agents can compose complex UIs purely through string concatenation and proxy state mapping.
options.tradeoffs: Significant upfront architectural investment required to achieve Article IV (Complete, No MVP) compliance before the ecosystem is actually useful to the agents.

options.title: Self-Healing, Auto-Mutating Interfaces
options.description: Leverage ArrowJS's minimal footprint (zero dependencies) to allow agents to read the entire UI codebase in a single context window. Agents can autonomously detect visual bugs, mutate the ArrowJS templates, and instantly verify the fix via COMET.
options.tradeoffs: Constant UI mutation can disorient human users. Requires rigorous, automated visual regression testing to ensure the 'healing' process doesn't introduce new regressions.

options.title: Hybrid React/ArrowJS Co-existence
options.description: Embed ArrowJS widgets within the existing React architecture, using ArrowJS only for the highly dynamic, agent-generated micro-frontends while keeping React for the static application shell.
options.tradeoffs: Introduces competing state management paradigms (React state vs. ArrowJS proxies). Muddying the UI architecture increases cognitive load for code-generation agents and risks synchronization bugs.
